description: core §7.5, a snapshot's pages. Written by an independent reading of the text (Python, standard library), checked, never blessed. A page's bytes are the whole GET reply's payload, CH to the last tombstone; its envelope parses as §7.5's snapshot on a put (`envelope/vectors.json` holds the envelope's refusals), and its body is what is read here. A page is `tag`, `run_width` (16 or 32) and `run` (CH's and the header's), `asof`, `time` (`{"s": t32, "ms": ms16}`, or `null` for the unknown time, t32 all ones and ms16 0), `index` and `more` (the page integer is index × 2 + more), `coll`, `live` and `tombs`. A live entry is `id` (a string, empty for the reply's key itself), `run_width` and `run` (`null` for the header's run), `seq`, `confirmation` (`none` for 0, the collection with no horizon; `time` for 1, vouched for at the snapshot's time; `conf` for 2, with `conf`, the last confirmation, a time or `null`) and `record` in hex. A tombstone is `id`, `run_width`, `run` and `seq`. A snapshot, in `pages`, is a page without `index` and `more`. `writes`: a page → its bytes in `hex` and their `size`, or the writer's refusal `{"refused": token}`, a token of the reading's for what it would refuse. `reads`: a page's bytes in hex → the page, or `{"refused": token}`, the first that applies reading the fields in order, and for one field the first in this list: `short` (the body ends before a byte a field needs, an integer's last byte included), `leb128` (an integer whose fifth byte has its high bit set, above 2^32 − 1, or not in its shortest form), `time` (a time or a conf with ms16 above 999, or t32 all ones with ms16 not 0), `id` (an id neither empty nor plain chunks joined by `/`), `order` (an id not above the one before it in its list, or a tombstone's id that a live entry of the body has), `flags` (a bit from 3 to 0 set, bit 4 without bit 7, confirmation 3, or a tombstone's confirmation other than 0), `run` (an entry's own run that is the header's, in width and value), `trailing` (a byte after the last tombstone). Every page read writes back to its bytes, and every page written reads back to its value. `pages`: a snapshot and a page size in bytes → the pages' bytes in order and their sizes, or the writer's refusal. The entries, live and tombstones together in the byte order of their ids, fill page 0, then page 1: a page takes the next entry when it holds none yet, or when its bytes with that entry are within the page size. The last page's more bit is 0, and a snapshot with no entry is one page. Every set of pages reads back, page by page, to the snapshot's entries.
